key_insight: A flow-based generative model can learn a practical approximation of the turbulent channel-flow phase-space distribution, enabling physically consistent synthetic turbulence and flow reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven route to generate realistic turbulent inflow fields and initial conditions for DNS, potentially reducing reliance on handcrafted turbulence synthesis.
method: Train a flow-based generative model on a minimal conditional flow unit at Reτ=180.
Sample conditional and unconditional turbulent fields using a consistent learned-distribution procedure.
Test whether generated fields preserve statistics, conditional consistency, and dynamical invariance.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated against direct numerical simulation and reproduced key statistics and dynamics, including intermittency, nonlinear energy transfer, and stationary ensemble behavior when used as DNS initial conditions.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated for turbulent channel flow at Reτ=180, so broader generalization to other Reynolds numbers, geometries, or flow regimes still needs verification.
paper_title: A machine-learned probability distribution in the phase space of turbulent channel flow for synthetic turbulence and flow reconstruction
